assumptions.text: Product name assumed as 'FamilyHub' from the source document's own title — not independently confirmed.
One administrator per family assumed sufficient for MVP.
Shopping-list write conflicts default to last-write-wins for MVP; source explicitly flags this must stay an explicit decision.
Purchased shopping items stay visible until explicitly cleared, per stated preference; source also lists this as an open question needing confirmation.
MVP recurrence limited to daily/weekly/monthly patterns only.
Backend web framework unspecified; source explicitly defers this to the architecture phase.
Backend runtime assumed Node.js-family (TypeScript is fixed, but the specific framework is not decided).
Expo-managed workflow assumed sufficient for most of MVP; bare/native config assumed necessary later for background location + push.

open_questions.text: Can one user belong to several families?
Can a child have an account? Can a child profile exist without an account?
Who can invite family members? Who can remove a member?
What happens when an event participant leaves the family? What happens to tasks assigned to a removed member? What should happen to a family when its administrator leaves?
Can children create calendar events? Can children see all family events?
How should recurring calendar events be represented — instances generated dynamically, or ahead of time?
Editing a recurring event: this occurrence only, this-and-future, or the entire series — which (if any) should MVP support?
Should calendar events support attachments?
Should the app support multiple time zones? How should DST changes be handled?
Beyond the tentative last-write-wins default, is there a better simultaneous-edit resolution to commit to?
Should shopping-list changes generate notifications, and if so batched how?
Exact authorization model: who can see whose location (parent-child, child-child)? Can a parent disable a child's sharing? How is a child's consent represented?
Should location sharing expire automatically?
How often should location update, and should updates happen in the background?
Should the server retain even the latest known location, or is that already too much?
Should family members be notified when someone starts/stops sharing their location?
Offline support: implement broadly, explicitly defer, or design-for-but-implement-only-shopping?
How should conflicting offline changes be merged?
What is the minimum viable notification system across all four feature areas?
Should there be a web client at all, beyond a possible later small admin interface?
Should data be encrypted at rest?
How long should location data be retained, if any is retained at all?
How can a user export their data? How can a user delete their account and all family data?
Exact location update-frequency strategy (normal vs. battery-saving modes).
Where precisely Expo-managed capabilities suffice vs. where native configuration becomes required.
Backend web framework choice — explicitly deferred to the architecture phase.
Eventual realtime mechanism (WebSockets vs. an alternative).
Whether data should be encrypted at rest.
Which MVP vertical slice should be built first — shared shopping lists or the family calendar?
Should the five pre-planned workflow-benchmark change requests run strictly after a stable MVP, or be interleaved?
